title: Record collecting and a stolen McKinney's Cotton Pickers record
summary: They talk about collectors who never listen and Steinau's record bought in Shanghai in 1946 that was stolen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, you know, this was before there was a really established emphasis on jazz criticism.
We assumed that we knew more than anybody else around was likely to. I'm still not convinced that we didn't.
Yeah, well, I, uh, not either. After all, some of the people who had huge collections also didn't go out and listen to live music.
Or I'm told that it had depressed him to go to some of these places like Lachim's.
And some people who had huge collections didn't listen to them. Oh, sure. You remember Tom Murray? Yeah. And his collection from which he had been separated for a number of years, I think. Mm-hmm.

Well, I mean, there's all kind of collecting. Yeah. There are people who collect labels, as we used to call those people, label collectors. Mm-hmm. They, uh, they didn't necessarily care about the records, the music on the records.

Of course, I remember one record in particular that disappeared about 1946 or 7. I'm still annoyed about. Must have been a little bit later. Which was a, which was a new copy of McKinney Cotton Pickers record that I had bought new in Shanghai, in 19, in Shanghai, China in 1946. It was the only jazz record they had in the shop. Mm-hmm. They had about 20 or 30 copies of the same record. How and why, I do not know. Oh, no. But somebody ripped it off, which annoyed the hell out of me.
Well, there's nothing like Friends. There are a lot of people who are collectors. Yeah. They just got like Friends.
